subject: Provisional lane request + priority clauses — Vega Health pilot
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional lane request + priority clauses — Vega Health pilot

Team,

Context: Vega Health (pilot account) wants a repeatable low-latency pilot starting the week of Sep 1 for 6 weeks. They want a dedicated slice with guardrails so their integration tests and parallel A/B experiments don't see noisy preemption. Sales previewed a $75K pilot commitment to cover part of infra.

Ask: before I loop legal + procurement, we need ops/product signoff on a provisional carve:
- Provision an ephemeral dedicated slice with a minimum of 4 GPU slots reserved for Vega for the first 2 weeks, with an option to scale to 12 GPUs for peak runs (on approval).
- Temporarily suspend the usual preemption window for this slice (i.e., mark as priority "pilot" for the duration).
- Grant an autoscale exception: allow manual bumping above the committed min without triggering reservation re-eval for 72 hours.

We need: capacity feasibility + estimated cost/run rate + list of any technical mitigations required to preserve latency SLO. Please review the attached pilot MAP and pricing-outline and send your recommended conditions by EOD Jul 31. If feasible, I will ask Sales to include the clause in the pilot MOU and route to procurement.

Attachments: vega-pilot-MAP.xlsx, pricing-outline.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

(On a separate note, Vega's engineering lead is Jay Patel — they may send a short technical checklist next week.)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional lane request + priority clauses — Vega Health pilot

Kimberly — thanks for the heads up. Quick notes after a first-pass inventory: 

- Current Q3 committed pools already have narrow headroom across us-west zones; guaranteeing 4 GPUs for a multi-week window would require either (a) temporary reallocation from soft-reserve pools or (b) an override carve from our staging buffer. Both have downstream impact on queued eval jobs.
- If we do a conditional carve, it should be time-bounded and include a release signal (e.g., invoice paid + performance checklist) to avoid long tail occupancy.

I attached a quick capacity-impact.csv with two scenarios: (A) 4 GPU carve for 14 days (minimal disruption) and (B) staged scale 4->8->12 with warm-up (moderate disruption). Estimated incremental cost (infra-only, rough):
- Scenario A: +$18k for 2 weeks (includes prewarm overhead)
- Scenario B: +$45k if they scale to 12 for <72 hours during test windows (includes burst buffer)

Questions for Product/Infra:
- Marcus: can you confirm whether we can mark the slice as non-preemptible at the hypervisor or scheduler level without breaking higher-priority SLAs?
- Aditya: are you comfortable with the invoice+MOU gating approach, or do you want a different procurement trigger?

If you want, I can reserve a tentative carve and tag it with an ops runbook that auto-releases if not confirmed by Aug 10.

Attachments: capacity-impact.csv

—David
David Kim
Capacity & Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provisional lane request + priority clauses — Vega Health pilot

Thanks — adding technical input and mitigations.

Summary: we can support a provisional 4 GPU carve with the following constraints and recommended mitigations to meet low-latency expectations:
1) Model variant: recommend serving a quantized 16-bit variant (Q4_0) for pilot runs — reduces memory footprint and speeds cold starts. We'll need model onboarding work (1 dev, ~3 days).
2) Prewarm & KV cache: allocate prewarmed containers with persistent KV cache priming for top 3 prompt flows Vega provided (we should ask Jay for representative traces).
3) Scheduler flag: we can mark the slice as "pilot-priority" which prevents opportunistic preemption but does not block emergency system-level evictions. This meets "no noisy preemption" for normal operations.
4) Staged scale plan: implement a scheduled scale window (4 -> 8 after week 2 -> 12 only during scheduled test windows). Autoscale exception should be manual via Ops-runbook with an automated rollback at 72h unless explicitly extended.

Risk notes: priority marking increases tail risk for other customers if capacity tightens — ops should keep a 24h notice window if global cluster pressure > 85%. Also, quantized variant carries a small quality delta (~1–2% on our eval prompts). If Vega requires bit-for-bit parity, we should decline quantization.

Estimate: infra engineering + ops labor for the onboarding and runbook (~40 engineer-hours) + prewarm & burst cost =~ $22k for the first two weeks. If they exercise full 12 GPU burst windows repeatedly, expect an additional ~$55k.

I'll prepare a short runbook template; David, please confirm the auto-release conditions.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Provisional lane request + priority clauses — Vega Health pilot

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Decision summary and next steps: 

1) Conditional approval: Ops will provision an ephemeral dedicated slice with a 4 GPU min for an initial 14-day pilot window starting Sep 1.
2) Scaling and priority: We accept the staged scale (4 -> 8 -> 12) with manual Ops-triggered bumps and a 72-hour automated rollback unless procurement confirms extension. The slice will be marked "pilot-priority" (per Marcus) — not absolute non-preemptible.
3) Billing & gating: Sales (Aditya) to include a pilot MOU with a partial prepayment (50% of estimated two-week infra run rate) and a DocuSign clause that invoice triggers the full carve. Aditya, please coordinate with Procurement to prepare the DocuSign link.
4) Quality & mitigations: Marcus to onboard the quantized model variant and deliver the runbook docx (attach to shared Drive). Quantization is acceptable for pilot; if Vega flags quality regressions, we'll fall back to full-precision and revisit costs.
5) Ops guardrail: David to put a tentative carve in place and set the auto-release for Aug 10 if not confirmed. Ops will monitor cluster pressure and provide a 24h notice if pressure >85%.

Kimberly will loop in Legal if Aditya confirms the MOU language. I uploaded the runbook draft to the shared folder and started a DocuSign envelope (link below). Please reply with any objections by EOD Aug 3; otherwise I will sign-off and hand to Sales.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/signed/VEGA-REQ-2025-07
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VegaPilotShare

Attachments: runbook-dedicated-slice.docx

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
